channel.title: The Indicator from Planet Money
channel.description:
A bite-sized show about big ideas. From the people who make Planet Money, The Indicator helps you make sense of what's happening in today's economy. It's a quick hit of insight into money, work, and business. Monday through Friday, in 10 minutes or less.
Sign up for our newsletter.

Support public media by joining NPR+ at plus.npr.org. You’ll get perks for over 25 NPR podcasts, including bonus episodes for Planet Money and sponsor-free listening for The Indicator.

item.title: Is it time to abolish the MBA?
item.description:
Does business school fix the world? Or does it just churn out consultants, bankers and tech workers? A professor and a dean debate the value of the modern-day MBA.

Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.

item.title: Why Meta is giving you Muse for free
item.description:

Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.

item.title: Can a "moneyball" system work for campaign funding?
item.description:
Elections are more expensive than ever, but are campaign donations going to the races where they’ll make the most impact? Today, we talk to the startup co-founder of Oath who believes there’s a smarter way to allocate individual donations.

Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.

item.title: The case for sharing your salary
item.description:
Should money and class figure more prominently in how we identify ourselves? Pulitzer Prize-winning data journalist Mona Chalabi thinks yes. Today on the show, a conversation with Mona, author of the forthcoming book Ten Lives: How What We Have Shapes Who We Are.

Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.
